documents.title: DD15 Won't Start Troubleshooting
documents.summary: TruckFixHub DD15 evidence: Separate no-crank from crank-no-start before replacing parts. If the engine cranks but will not start, verify adequate cranking speed and battery voltage; check fuel supply and investigate loss of prime, restriction, air intrusion or recent fuel-system work; use diagnostic data to verify the engine controller is seeing information required for starting; inspect accessible engine-harness connectors and wiring for damage, corrosion, loose terminals or recent disturbance; record SPN/FMI codes and determine which are active, and do not assume a component named by a code is automatically defective. If the no-start began after batteries, fuel filters, wiring, CPC/ECM work or another repair, begin by checking what changed. Missing module data, unusual dash behavior or multiple communication faults deserve electrical/network diagnosis before expensive engine parts are replaced. Do not bypass safety systems or loosen high-pressure fuel components to check for fuel.

documents.title: Cummins X15 Won't Start Troubleshooting
documents.summary: TruckFixHub X15 evidence: Separate no-crank from crank-no-start before chasing fuel or sensors. If the X15 cranks but will not start, verify cranking speed and battery voltage are adequate; check fuel supply, filters and recent fuel-system service and investigate restriction, air intrusion or loss of prime rather than guessing at expensive components; use diagnostic software/data to confirm the ECM is receiving the engine information needed during cranking; inspect accessible harnesses, connectors, power and grounds for damage, corrosion, looseness or recent disturbance; record all active Cummins fault information before clearing codes. If the problem began after a fuel-filter change, battery replacement, wiring repair or engine work, inspect what was just touched. Fuel-pressure and fuel-delivery complaints should be verified using applicable Cummins procedures and service information rather than treated as automatic component replacements. Do not bypass safety systems or loosen high-pressure fuel components to check for fuel.

documents.title: Semi-Truck Engine Cranks But Won't Start
documents.summary: TruckFixHub general crank-no-start evidence: A true crank-no-start means the engine is rotating at a reasonable cranking speed; slow or labored cranking points back toward batteries, cables, connections, starter load or mechanical resistance. Useful observations include whether it quit while driving or failed after shutdown, whether it attempts to fire, cranking speed consistency, warning/security messages, engine-controller communication, active SPN/FMI or manufacturer faults, plausible ECM engine speed while cranking, recent service, and known fuel level/condition. Diagnostic path: verify adequate battery voltage, cable integrity and cranking speed under load; verify engine-controller power and communication; evaluate engine-speed information using the exact engine OEM procedure; evaluate fuel supply restriction, air intrusion, priming, supply-pump operation, filters, commanded versus actual rail pressure and injector/control conditions as applicable to that engine; if electronic and fuel requirements are met, approved procedures may be needed for intake restriction, valve timing, compression or other mechanical causes. Required pressures and tests vary by engine family. Do not replace a crank sensor, fuel pump, injectors or ECM merely because those parts can cause a no-start; confirm the failed condition first. Follow OEM fuel-system safety procedures and do not use starting fluid unless specifically permitted by the manufacturer and approved procedure.
